title: Micro pipeline playbook — sandbox scratch
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for a small, composable response-pipeline playbook that a product or platform engineer can drop into a dev repo to compose cheap, testable micro-stages (retrieval, rewrite, filter, rerank, enrich). Aim: make it trivial to prototype chains locally, measure token/latency/cost impact, and have deterministic replay for debugging.

Why:
- Teams repeatedly build ad-hoc pipelines (retrieval + LLM + rerank) with duplicate infra and little reproducibility.
- Want a low-friction, batteries-included local dev loop (CLI + tiny server) that maps to Redwood serving configs (routes, batching, cache hints).

Goals (MVP):
- Minimal YAML pipeline manifest + container-like stage types (call-model, call-embed, call-retriever, deterministic-transform).
- Local CLI to run a pipeline against sample prompts and produce token/cost/latency breakdowns and a replayable request bundle.
- Cost simulator that estimates per-stage token cost using user-supplied model profiles (tokens per call, avg output tokens, quantized cost multipliers).
- Snapshotable state for each run (inputs, outputs, stage latency) allowing deterministic replay and unit tests.

User stories:
- As an engineer, I can define a 3-stage pipeline in a YAML file and run `micro-pipe run myflow.yml --sample tests/test1.json` to see a per-stage cost table and timeline.
- As an SRE, I can run `micro-pipe simulate --qps 50 --duration 60s` to validate that batching policies reduce per-token cost at certain throughput.
- As a PM, I can flag a stage as "fidelity-critical" so stage-level regression alerts can be generated against eval prompts.

Example pipeline manifest (sketch inside content):
```
pipeline: compact-search-rewrite
stages:
  - id: retrieve
    type: retriever
    config: { index: local-test-kv, top_k: 4 }
  - id: rewrite
    type: call-model
    config: { model: small-qa-1, prompt_template: rewrite-v1 }
  - id: rerank
    type: call-model
    config: { model: reranker-lite, scoring: cosine }
metrics:
  record: [tokens, latency_ms, cost_est_usd]
```

(above is pseudo-yaml, not strict)

Developer workflow (rough):
1) Create manifest + tests.
2) Run `micro-pipe run` which spins a local harness (no docker requirement) that wires simple in-memory retrievers and mocks for heavy stages (optional live model calls).
3) Inspect HTML report with waterfall chart, token table, and per-stage sample outputs.
4) `micro-pipe snapshot create` stores the run bundle (jsonl) for later replay and attaches to PR.

Telemetry & acceptance signals:
- Per-stage median latency and p95, tokens consumed, and cost delta vs baseline pipeline.
- Regression detection: if rewrite stage reduces retrieval hit rate below threshold, flag.
- UX signal: # of flows prototyped within 1 day and # promoted to hosted/route.

Tradeoffs / questions:
- How faithful should local sim be vs production (hardware differences)? Start coarse: per-token cost multipliers and measured latency profiles users can import/export.
- Should pipeline stage types map 1:1 with Redwood route configs? Prefer to map conceptually (call-model => route) but keep the manifest portable.
- Security: pipelines may contain secrets (API keys). Default: local-only encrypted store + recommend ephemeral keys.

Next experiments to try quickly:
- Integrate small-cost estimation with Redwood model catalog so `micro-pipe` can auto-fill cost params.
- Add a tiny web UI to reorder stages and compare diffs (before/after cost and quality).
- Run small internal hackathon: 10 engineers build a pipeline in a day; capture friction points.

To do (short):
- [ ] Prototype CLI scaffolding and manifest parser (Sam)
- [ ] Wire minimal retriever and simple prompt templates (Priya)
- [ ] Cost sim: map model profiles to per-token USD (Noah)
- [ ] Snapshot format and replay API (me)

Open probs / notes to self:
- Need deterministic RNG seeds in model mocks so unit tests are stable.
- Useful to include small "golden prompts" set per pipeline for quick quality checks.
- How to surface batching behavior in local sim? Maybe allow a synthetic QPS parameter and apply a simplified batching algorithm (group by model + route) to show theoretical savings.

References / inspiration:
- local-runtime-devkit notes (we should avoid duplicating; instead focus on playbook + cost-sim + snapshot)
- internal pipeline-starters repo PR above

Quick sketch of acceptance criteria for a first internal alpha: 
- Can author a pipeline and run 10 sample prompts locally, get a report with per-stage tokens/costs/latency, and produce a snapshot file.
- Snapshot replays produce bit-identical stage outputs for mocked stages.
- Basic cost-sim shows sensible deltas when toggling batching and changing model profiles.

If this feels useful, I will convert into a short PRD and a 2-week spike plan. For now: brain-dump mode.
